title: Extra shifts to pay the bills
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on an elderly care ward. Grace, a healthcare assistant, looks exhausted. When you ask if she's all right, she tells you she has been working extra bank shifts most days for a month to pay off debts, and is barely sleeping.

She asks you not to tell anyone.
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 5 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Tell her about the trust's financial wellbeing and staff support services.
options.brief: Practical support can help her address the cause.
options.detailed: Many trusts offer financial advice and hardship support. Knowing about them may help her reduce her hours. It ranks third because it's less immediate than supporting her and her health.

options.text: Listen, and ask how she is coping.
options.brief: She has confided in you and needs to feel heard.
options.detailed: Financial pressure and exhaustion are hard to talk about. Listening, without judgement, shows care and helps you understand how she is.

options.text: Encourage her to talk to her manager or occupational health about her hours.
options.brief: Her hours may be affecting her health and her work.
options.detailed: Working most days for a month while barely sleeping may affect her health and patient care. Her manager or occupational health can help, and she can choose to speak to them.

options.text: Tell her that her finances are none of your business.
options.detailed: You asked, and she confided in you. This is dismissive, and leaves her unsupported and possibly unsafe at work.

options.text: Offer to lend her some money.
options.detailed: This is generous, but lending money to a colleague can create difficulties, and doesn't address her debts or exhaustion.

explanation.issue: This tests how you support a colleague in financial difficulty whose exhaustion may affect her health and work.
explanation.keyDetails: She is exhausted and barely sleeping. The cause is financial. She asked you not to tell anyone.
explanation.reasoning: [B] listens, [C] encourages her to get help with her hours, and [A] offers practical support. [E] blurs boundaries, and [D] dismisses her.
explanation.competing: If her exhaustion were clearly putting patients at risk, you might need to raise it even without her agreement. At this stage, encouraging her to seek help is the right approach.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 3, supporting colleagues and acting when patient safety may be affected.
